title: Gallery Prototype C | Journey Board

hero.title: Journey
hero.subtitle: Board Narrative
hero.lead: This direction sits between a timeline and a storyboard. It is the strongest option if you want each milestone to feel like a chapter with room for mini-highlights, side notes, and future sub-links.
chips: Good balance of text and image

aside.title: How This Prototype Reads
aside.copy: The left rail explains the overall arc while the right side expands each stage into a chapter card. This is useful if some milestones later need more internal structure than a simple caption card.

legend.label: Supports clusters
legend.note: Projects can sit inside each chapter

legend.label: Future-proof
legend.note: Easy to add PDFs and work summaries

sidebar.title: Sample Arc
sidebar.copy: This prototype is less literal than the git graph and less image-heavy than the museum layout. It is useful if you want each stage to feel like a chapter with internal highlights.

nodes.title: 10th Standard
nodes.copy: The first chapter card introduces a stage and gives room for two or three supporting notes without making the page feel crowded.
bullets: Can hold a concise description of the period
Can point to an award, image, or memory block
Can later link to a dedicated detail page

nodes.title: 12th Standard
nodes.copy: This layout works well when the milestone needs a bit more structure than a normal card, such as notes, two small takeaways, and one related link.
bullets: Useful for exam, city, or institution shifts
Keeps the visual flow simple and readable

nodes.title: College
nodes.copy: The college stage becomes a central chapter. Later it can contain internal links to project pages, departments, posters, clubs, or a breakdown of what changed during that period.
bullets: Works as the main chapter split point
Allows multiple sub-highlights in one card
Can grow without breaking the page rhythm
nodes.mini_note: Add institution, years, or a signature note here.

nodes.title: Projects During College
nodes.copy: This chapter can later hold a small list of project titles or a grouped card pattern without needing a separate page redesign.
bullets: Best if some milestones contain several outputs
Can accommodate tags, posters, and screenshots
Lets you group related work by phase
nodes.mini_note: Add project tags or quick stats here.

nodes.title: Joined PhD
nodes.copy: The final chapter can later become the richest one: active themes, major achievements, posters, thesis links, or deeper routes into research containers.
bullets: Easy to connect with research and contact pages
nodes.mini_note: Add publications, poster links, or PhD focus here.

footer: this version is optimized for chapter-based storytelling and will be the easiest one to expand if your real content varies a lot in depth between milestones.
